messages:
Maya Chen: Following up on the PhoenixEdge postmortem. We identified three vectors: recurring VPC peering instability, on-prem NAT/conntrack exhaustion, and a tenant-cleanup race that left attachments orphaned. Need owners, short timelines, and customer mitigations.

Samir Patel: I can own the peering stability work. Steps: repro in staging, capture BGP flap traces, adjust keepalive/hold timers conservatively, and add a peer-health watchdog that temporarily blackholes flapping peers. Target: 10 business days. Will open RFC.

Priya Rao: I'll instrument the canary with an active peering probe and add an alert for jitter > 50ms and route churn > 3/hr. ETA 4 business days. Also will add a regression test to CI for route convergence.

Jorge Alvarez: I'll pin the on-prem checklist items. Immediate additions: conntrack table size guidance, NAT port reservation notes, and sample iptables conntrack tune commands. Will PR the checklist and notify Solutions. ETA: 48h.

Elaine Wu: I'll take the tenant cleanup bug. Plan: make cleanup idempotent using a short lease + backoff retry, add an integration test that simulates concurrent controller deletes, and include metrics for orphaned-attachments. Hoping to push a dedicated patch to the minor release next Tue.

Ron Keller: Short-term customer mitigation: limit control-plane concurrency for PhoenixEdge tenants and enable failover to the standby pool. Command to flip policy: 

```
redwoodctl policy set --customer phoenixedge --control-concurrency 4 --fallback standby-pool
```

This reduces throughput but prevents churn. Use with customer consent. :warning:
